I will put all 10.9 mu into cotton again this year because that is the crop I know best, it fits my land and water conditions, and with only two people in the household I will keep the plan simple and manageable. Since it is the start of the growing season, I will prepare the field with rotary tillage because it is less labor-intensive than deep ploughing and is enough for my cotton ground. I will use improved seed rather than traditional seed because I want steadier emergence and yield, but I will avoid making the system too complicated. For fertilizer, I will use a moderate rate: enough nitrogen to support vegetative growth and boll setting, with phosphorus and potassium to support rooting, plant strength, and boll development. Because I have well irrigation, I will irrigate several times through the season, mainly around establishment, flowering, and boll formation, but I will not overwater. I will spray pesticides when pressure appears, especially for insects and disease risk in the main growth period, and I expect a solid but not extreme yield because I would rather manage steadily than chase very high input production.
